componentPlan.focusQuote: Once your teen has a steady job, help them set up a savings program so that at least 10 percent of earnings goes directly into their savings account.
componentPlan.pedagogicalReason: Checks core savings rules and emergency fund purpose before exploring growth examples.

componentPlan.focusQuote: However, if they begin saving at age 35, they’d have about $7,000 at age 65.
componentPlan.pedagogicalReason: Contrasts early and late starters on shared saving terms to show timing effects.

overview.headline: Teens build emergency savings and grow money early with interest

keyPoints.point: Teens should save 10 percent of earnings to build emergency savings for living expenses
keyPoints.quote: to save 10 percent of what you earn, and have at least three months’ worth of living expenses saved up in case of an emergency.

keyPoints.point: Emergency savings help avoid relying on credit cards or loans that charge high interest
keyPoints.quote: can help your child avoid having to rely on credit cards or loan options that charge a high interest rate

keyPoints.point: Compound interest earns interest on saved money and previously earned interest so early saving grows
keyPoints.quote: Compound interest is when your child earns interest on both the money they save and the interest they earn.

keyPoints.point: Saving every year starting early lets interest build from prior interest over time
keyPoints.quote: If they set aside $100 every year starting at age 14, they’d have about $23,000 at age 65.

keyTerms.gloss: safe place to keep money for emergencies
keyTerms.quote: Having money in a savings account can help your child avoid having to rely on credit cards

keyTerms.gloss: interest earned on saved money and on earlier interest
keyTerms.quote: Compound interest is when your child earns interest on both the money they save and the interest they earn.

keyTerms.gloss: price for borrowing money that matters less for emergency savings
keyTerms.quote: the interest rate may not be as relevant since the goal is to save enough money to cover emergency expenses

keyTerms.gloss: retirement account offered through work with possible employer matching
keyTerms.quote: they may be offered a retirement account at work called a 401(k).

analysis.pageCoverage: Teen saving habits, emergency funds in insured accounts, retirement matching basics, and early compound growth with bank research activities.
